notes.text: Saint Stephen was chosen when Greek-speaking widows were being neglected in the early Jerusalem community's daily food distribution.
Saint Stephen's public arguments made him a target because his preaching challenged powerful assumptions about law, temple, and faith.
Acts says Saint Stephen prayed for forgiveness for his attackers while he was being killed.
Saul of Tarsus, later known as Paul the Apostle, appears in Acts as a witness approving Saint Stephen's death.
Saint Stephen became known in Christian tradition as the protomartyr, meaning the first martyr.
